title: Plan and validate lambda-only cutover
description: Deploy to a named test stack and verify login, registration, upload, list, analyze, tracing, audit/admin, static assets, and health checks on that stack hostname. Define rollback steps for a failed stack validation or in-place stack update; the migration does not depend on moving a shared production DNS record.
acceptance_criteria: A named lambda-only stack passes the smoke flows on its own hostname; rollback steps are documented for failed stack validation or in-place stack update; the previous known-good stack remains available until the new stack is accepted.
notes:
After the initial PR #1113 implementation, make sam-build passes and reports LambdaResizeFunction 219MB and LambdaWebFunction 64MB unzipped. Remaining validation for this cutover task: run SAM-local or non-production deployed route smoke for web, resize, static assets, login/registration/upload/list/analyze/tracing/admin flows, then document rollback before production DNS changes.
Cutover runbook drafted in docs/Development/LambdaWebMigration.rst. Local validation passed: strict Sphinx, make template-lint, make sam-deploy-version-check, and git diff --check. Actual non-production stack validation is not started because the branch has unpushed commits that make sam-build refuse, and samconfig.toml currently targets dev-stack while using planttracer-prod / DynamoDBTablePrefix=prod parameters; confirm intended test resources before deployment.
Updated SAM config guidance: document that SAM config is per-stack local deploy state, recommend one ignored config file per stack rather than profiles in a shared file, and adjust Makefile targets to honor SAM_CONFIG while refusing tracked config files. Validated strict Sphinx, make template-lint, make sam-version-check, make sam-deploy-version-check, SAM_CONFIG=.samconfig.example.toml make sam-config-path-check, and git diff --check.
Replaced local .sam-last-deployed-version deploy guard with deployed stack inspection: Makefile now resolves ApplicationUrl/LambdaDnsName from CloudFormation, reads /api/ver, refuses same-version deploys only when the deployed version is readable, and warns/allows first deploys or broken-stack recovery. Refusal message and docs now explain that version bumps matter because lambda-web SnapStart snapshots published Lambda versions.
Source-side cutover planning is committed-ready: SAM config handling is local/ignored, same-version deploy guard now inspects deployed /api/ver and tolerates broken stacks, and runbook documents smoke/rollback. Remaining acceptance requires a pushed branch plus non-production stack deployment and manual smoke checks.
Non-production slgstack validation found live deployment issues: https://slgstack.planttracer.com/ returns Flask 404; /about, /ver, /api/ver, and /static/planttracer.js also return the same 404; /ping returns 'Healthy Connection', which is not present in current source or local SAM build; /resize-api/v1/ping returns JSON from lambda-resize. Local Makefile-driven lambda-web tests for /ping, /static/planttracer.js, /ver, and /api/ver pass, and the local SAM build artifact contains the current Flask root and /ping routes. AWS CLI inspection is blocked until SSO is refreshed; next validation step is to inspect CloudFormation routes, LambdaWebFunction handler/version/alias, environment, and CloudWatch logs for slgstack.
Implemented resize ping deployment metadata for validation: /resize-api/v1/ping now reports app_version and deployed_at. Makefile stamps the built lambda-resize artifact before sam-deploy/sam-deploy-guided, and sam-status displays the reported fields when available.
Diagnosed live /api/ver 404: direct invoke of LambdaWebFunction:live with rawPath=/api/ver returns 200 from api_ver, while execute-api /prod/api/ver reaches Lambda but Flask 404s. Root cause is HTTP API named-stage prefix in rawPath. lambda-web now strips the requestContext.stage prefix before passing payload-format-2.0 events to apig_wsgi; tests cover /prod/api/ver and /prod root.
Implemented Powertools for lambda-web where it fits the current Flask bridge: lambda_web.main now uses aws_lambda_powertools Logger and APIGatewayProxyEventV2 for HTTP API v2 request parsing/diagnostics, while keeping apig-wsgi for the actual Flask WSGI handoff because Powertools' API Gateway resolver is a native Lambda router rather than a Flask WSGI adapter. Lambda-web requirements and template env now include Powertools.
Correction from July 5 discussion: there is no shared production DNS cutover for this migration. Each stack is brought up on a distinct hostname for testing, so remaining validation is stack-hostname smoke plus rollback/keep-previous-stack guidance rather than Route53 production DNS movement.

title: Define one-host HTTP front-door routing
description: Define one public HTTPS front door for the application. Route /resize-api/* to lambda-resize. Route HTML pages, Flask /api/*, and /static/* to lambda-web for the initial migration. Preserve or intentionally migrate /api/v1/movie-data compatibility. Record that separate S3/CloudFront static hosting is deferred until versioned asset names, an asset manifest, or a cache invalidation strategy is designed.
design: Decision: the lambda-only distribution should not require one public domain name per Lambda. Use one public HTTPS hostname for the product and route by path: lambda-web serves Flask HTML, Flask /api/*, and /static/*; lambda-resize serves /resize-api/* vision/video work. Static files remain packaged with and served by lambda-web for the initial migration, matching current Flask behavior. title: Plan lambda-only Plant Tracer distribution
description:
## Lambda-only migration goals

1. **Eliminate the production VM from the SAM distribution.** The deployed stack should not create EC2, VPC, subnet, security-group, EIP, instance-profile, SSH, or VM reload resources.
2. **Replace boot-time branch checkout with built artifacts from the current branch.** Remove the SAM `GitBranch`/`GitRepoUrl` model because Lambda deployment packages are built before deployment.
3. **Run the interaction web app in a separate `lambda-web` function.** Keep the existing Flask route code where practical and adapt it to API Gateway rather than rewriting the application router first.
4. **Keep `lambda-resize` as the vision/video Lambda.** It already owns frame extraction, tracing, SQS trace work, and video/movie-data routes; do not merge web traffic into the vision package.
5. **Expose the system through one public HTTPS hostname.** The two Lambda functions do not need separate product domains; the front door should route HTML, Flask `/api/*`, and `/static/*` to `lambda-web`, and `/resize-api/*` to `lambda-resize`.
6. **Keep application static assets served by `lambda-web` for the initial migration.** Static files stay packaged with the web Lambda and are not moved to S3/CloudFront until there is a versioned-asset or manifest plan.
7. **Keep durable data external to stack replacement.** DynamoDB tables remain created by `src/dbutil.py` from `etc/dynamodb_tables.json`; the movie S3 bucket remains pre-existing and long-lived.
8. **Preserve the browser/API contract during cutover.** HTML, Flask `/api/*`, `/static/*`, and `/resize-api/*` must route predictably; `/api/v1/movie-data` compatibility must be handled deliberately.
9. **Keep the Makefile as the only supported local/test/deploy entrypoint.** New Lambda build, static publish, smoke, lint, and test workflows should be Makefile targets.
10. **Document and verify the migration as a production architecture change.** Docs, tests, and deployment smoke checks must prove behavior, not just template shape.

## Implementation issue list

1. **Document the lambda-only target architecture.**
   - Update `docs/Development/LambdaWebMigration.rst` from design discussion to implementation plan.
   - Record no-VM, current-branch artifact deployment, `lambda-web` plus `lambda-resize`, external DynamoDB/S3 ownership, and Lambda-served static assets.
   - Update architecture/local-development/environment docs touched by the plan.

2. **Add the `lambda-web` Flask adapter package.**
   - Add a Lambda handler that wraps the existing Flask app through `apig-wsgi`.
   - Keep route behavior in `src/app/flask_app.py` and `src/app/flask_api.py`.
   - Add Lambda-safe status/diagnostic behavior without requiring a `.git` checkout.

3. **Split web and vision Lambda dependencies and artifacts.**
   - Add explicit web Lambda requirements/export/build targets.
   - Keep OpenCV/PyAV/video dependencies out of the `lambda-web` artifact.
   - Keep shared app-code packaging explicit for both Lambda functions.

4. **Rewrite `template.yaml` as a lambda-only stack.**
   - Remove EC2/VPC/EIP/security group/instance profile/SSH resources and outputs.
   - Remove `GitRepoUrl`, `GitBranch`, keypair, AMI, and instance type parameters.
   - Add `lambda-web` function, IAM role, log group, environment variables, and route bindings.
   - Keep one public HTTPS front door; route HTML, Flask `/api/*`, and `/static/*` to `lambda-web`, and `/resize-api/*` to `lambda-resize`.
   - Keep `lambda-resize`, SQS, external S3 movie bucket parameter, external DynamoDB prefix, and scoped IAM.

5. **Keep static assets served by `lambda-web` until versioning exists.**
   - Package `src/app/static` with the web Lambda and preserve current Flask static serving behavior.
   - Do not add S3/CloudFront static hosting in the first lambda-only migration.
   - Create a later static-hosting/versioning plan before any move to long-lived cached static assets.
   - Ensure application static assets remain distinct from user-uploaded movie storage.

6. **Define and test HTTP front-door routing.**
   - Use one public HTTPS hostname for the application.
   - Route `/resize-api/*` to `lambda-resize`.
   - Route HTML and Flask `/api/*` to `lambda-web`.
   - Route `/static/*` to `lambda-web` for the initial migration.
   - Record that S3/CloudFront static hosting is deferred until asset filenames are versioned or an asset manifest/cache invalidation strategy exists.
   - Preserve or intentionally migrate `/api/v1/movie-data` compatibility.

7. **Normalize browser URL and static asset helpers.**
   - Replace scattered `url_for('static', ...)`/`./static/...` assumptions with one helper or convention.
   - Keep `API_BASE`, same-origin `/static/*`, and `LAMBDA_API_BASE` coherent locally and in AWS.
   - Defer `PLANTTRACER_STATIC_BASE` or external static-origin support until the versioning plan exists.

8. **Update Makefile deployment and smoke tooling.**
   - Make `sam-build` build both Lambda artifacts from the current checkout.
   - Remove deploy-guided prompts for EC2 keypairs and git branches.
   - Update `sam-status`, log helpers, and smoke checks for web Lambda, resize Lambda, and static assets.

9. **Add behavior-focused lambda-web tests.**
   - Test `/ping`, `/ver`, one public page, one authenticated page, and one Flask `/api/*` endpoint through the Lambda handler.
   - Use DynamoDB Local and MinIO fixtures; do not mock AWS storage.
   - Ensure tests fail when local prerequisites are missing.

10. **Verify package boundaries and production readiness.**
    - Check `lambda-web` artifact excludes vision/video dependencies.
    - Check both Lambda artifacts remain under AWS size limits.
    - Validate SAM/cfn-lint, docs, lint, and focused tests through Makefile targets.

11. **Handle mail/secrets for Lambda.**
    - Decide SES IAM vs Secrets Manager-backed SMTP for `lambda-web`.
    - Move VM environment-file assumptions into Lambda parameters/secrets.
    - Smoke-test registration and resend-login in a non-production stack.

12. **Plan and execute cutover/rollback validation.**
    - Deploy to a non-production stack first.
    - Verify login, registration, upload, list, analyze, tracing, audit/admin, static assets, and health checks.
    - Define rollback steps before production DNS moves to Lambda.

13. **Update project instructions and release-facing docs.**
    - Update `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` with Beads workflow and lambda-only migration rules.
    - Update `ReleaseHistory.rst` when the migration ships.
    - Flag tutorial screenshots if visible URLs or flows change.
notes: PR #1113 implementation pass initiated the Lambda-only stack: lambda-web adapter added, SAM template rewritten without VM resources/branch parameters, static assets kept on lambda-web, Makefile packaging/smoke targets updated, local Flask pytest path preserved, and local validation gates pass. Remaining open work: sam-build artifact sizing, SAM-local or deployed route smoke, mail/secrets validation, cutover/rollback, URL-helper cleanup, and later static-shell/API-auth decisions.

title: Plan cookie-based API auth and REST method cleanup
description:
Drafted by Codex from the lambda-only migration planning discussion.

## Context

The current API design uses POST broadly because `api_key` is often sent as a form/query parameter and the code comments say this avoids writing the key into URL logs. The current code also already supports an `api_key` cookie via `apikey.get_user_api_key()`, and login routes set that cookie from `?api_key=...` login links.

The lambda-only target has one public HTTPS front door. If browser API authentication is cookie-based on that same origin, the browser can send the credential as a cookie instead of putting `api_key` in URLs or form bodies.

## Question

Should browser APIs move to cookie/header-based authentication and then restore normal HTTP method semantics: GET for safe reads, POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE for mutations?

## Initial assessment

This is worth tracking as a separate security/API cleanup issue. It should not block the first lambda-only migration, but it directly affects the API contract and should be planned before broad API route cleanup.

Important constraints:

- Query-string `api_key` should be removed from browser fetch URLs such as first-frame and movie-data requests.
- Form/body `api_key` should stop being required for same-origin browser calls once the cookie path is canonical.
- The login-link flow still needs a token in the URL initially, but the server should consume it, set the cookie, and redirect to a clean URL.
- If the auth cookie is sent automatically, mutating endpoints need CSRF protection or an explicit decision that `SameSite`, method choices, and custom headers are sufficient.
- Logs must not capture the `Cookie` header or authorization header in API Gateway, CloudFront, Flask, or Lambda logs.
- Non-browser clients may still need a documented header, such as `X-API-Key`, rather than a cookie.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document the target authentication contract for browser calls, non-browser clients, and login links.
- Decide whether the `api_key` cookie should become `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite=Lax` or stricter.
- Define CSRF protection for mutating endpoints before relying on cookie auth.
- Inventory endpoints that can safely become GET once secrets are no longer in URLs.
- Update API docs and tests as part of any implementation.

Refs #699.
acceptance_criteria: Decision records the browser and non-browser API auth contract, cookie flags, CSRF stance, endpoint method inventory, log-safety requirements, docs impact, and tests before implementation begins.
notes: Per project scope review, this cookie-based API auth and REST method cleanup is not part of the lambda-only migration work. Keep it as a future API/security cleanup item, separate from completing PR #1113 / issue #699.
close_reason: Out of scope for the lambda-only migration project. Cookie-based API auth and REST method cleanup may be revisited as a separate future API/security effort, not as part of PR #1113 / issue #699.

title: Evaluate static HTML shell architecture for lambda-only web app
description:
Drafted by Codex from the lambda-only migration planning discussion.

## Context

Issue #699 is moving Plant Tracer to a lambda-only distribution with `lambda-web` and `lambda-resize`. For the initial migration, static assets remain packaged with `lambda-web` and served from `/static/*` by Flask/Lambda, as they are today. They should not move to S3/CloudFront until the project has a versioned filename, asset manifest, or cache-invalidation plan.

Today `lambda-web` would still render HTML pages with Jinja2. The current code uses `render_template(..., **page_dict(...))` for public pages and authenticated pages, and `page_dict()` injects runtime values such as `API_BASE`, `STATIC_BASE`, `lambda_api_base`, `api_key`, user identity, admin state, demo mode, and movie state constants.

## Question

Should the HTML pages eventually become static shells, with dynamic state fetched through JSON APIs, instead of being rendered by Flask/Jinja2 on each page request?

## Initial assessment

This is worth evaluating, but it should not block the first lambda-only migration. Keeping Jinja2 in `lambda-web` initially preserves the current browser contract, login flow, authenticated-page behavior, static asset serving, and template/global injection while we remove the VM.

Moving to static HTML shells could reduce `lambda-web` page-render invocations and improve cacheability, especially for public pages. However, it requires a deliberate browser contract and should be considered together with the future static asset versioning plan:

- A static runtime configuration source, such as `/static/config.json` or a tiny `/api/config` response.
- A session/current-user endpoint, such as `/api/session`, to replace server-side `page_dict()` injection.
- A decision about admin/demo/menu state that is currently rendered into templates.
- A migration path for login links and authenticated pages such as `/list`, `/upload`, `/analyze`, `/audit`, and `/users`.
- A versioned asset or manifest strategy before relying on long-lived static caching outside `lambda-web`.
- Tests proving that static shells plus JSON APIs preserve current behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Inventory all Jinja templates and classify them as static public pages, static authenticated shells, or pages that should remain server-rendered.
- Define the replacement contract for `page_dict()` browser globals.
- Decide whether static-shell migration is incremental after lambda-only cutover or part of a later release.
- Coordinate with the static asset versioning plan before any move to S3/CloudFront or long-lived external static caching.
- Produce a concrete implementation plan with affected docs and tests.

Refs #699 and #1110.
acceptance_criteria: Decision records whether static HTML shells should replace Jinja-rendered pages now, incrementally after lambda-only cutover, or not at all; includes template inventory, page_dict replacement contract, static asset versioning dependency, docs impact, and test plan.
notes: Decision recorded in docs/Development/LambdaWebMigration.rst: keep Jinja-rendered pages for the initial lambda-only migration; defer static HTML shells until cookie/API cleanup and versioned static assets exist. Added template inventory, page_dict replacement contract, docs impact, and test plan. Validated strict Sphinx and git diff --check.
close_reason: Static HTML shell decision documented: defer static-shell migration until after lambda-only cutover, cookie/API cleanup, and versioned static asset plan; template inventory and replacement contract recorded.
